items.title: Labor's 'ambitious' plan for tax reset
items.description: Labor will raise taxes on investment properties and some trust funds, giving the revenue back to workers with a new $250 tax break unveiled in the federal budget.

items.title: Find out if you're among the budget's winners or losers
items.description: In the first full budget since Labor's landslide election victory last year, the government is putting some money back in workers' pockets and increasing taxes on investors. So who wins and who misses out?

items.title: Australia's last baby boomer prime minister becomes King of the Kids
items.description: Tonight, Anthony Albanese becomes the first serving prime minister in decades to take a hammer to the most sacred shibboleth in Australian domestic politics.

items.title: How CGT changes could push investors to look outside property
items.description: Investors in stocks will be affected by changes to capital gains tax, but experts say the budget is still likely to see some investment move away from property and into shares.

items.title: Treasurer on broken election promises in the budget
items.description: Jim Chalmers says he won't be surprised if there's backlash over broken election promises in the federal budget. Speaking to 7.30, the treasurer says the decision to change negative gearing and the capital gains tax discount was only taken "in recent weeks".

items.title: UK PM Starmer faces more calls to quit as ministers resign
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer is striking a defiant tone despite a growing number of his Labour colleagues urging him to step down.

items.title: Government accused of 'burying' response to landmark gambling report
items.description: A long-awaited response to an inquiry that called for a gambling advertising ban has been tabled on budget day, prompting accusations the government is trying to bury the document.

items.title: Jacinta Nampijinpa Price leads emotional tributes for Kumanjayi Little Baby
items.description: Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price weeps through an impassioned tribute to her niece, Kumanjayi Little Baby, in federal parliament, amid a push to broaden the focus of an inquiry announced in the wake of her alleged murder.

items.title: Anti-Indian hate on the rise in New Zealand
items.description: Indian communities across New Zealand say they are feeling "hounded" after a surge in racist incidents.

items.title: Record payout after billionaire built mine without traditional owners' permission
items.description: Andrew Forrest's Fortescue has been ordered to pay $150 million to WA traditional owners after mining their land without permission.

items.title: Property owner says he helped wounded officer after Dezi Freeman shot at police
items.description: A Porepunkah property owner says he helped a wounded police officer after the fatal shooting when Dezi Freeman killed two Victoria police officers.

items.title: The name of this health condition was 'very inaccurate'. Now it's changed
items.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has been renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), a move health experts say will lead to faster diagnoses and better treatment for women of all ages.

items.title: My four-year break from booze has led to an unexpected discovery
items.description: What started out as abstinence during a pregnancy four years ago turned into a game with myself to see how long I could go without alcohol.

items.title: 'We are being attacked': Frantic call from a sailor to his family
items.description: As a peace deal between the US and Iran remains elusive, low-wage seafarers are in limbo as they witness an unprecedented 21st-century battle.

items.title: Australian Jewish women experiencing mass antisemitism, research says
items.description: About 80 per cent of Jewish women in Australia have experienced antisemitism personally or against an immediate family member in the past two years, the royal commission has heard.

items.title: Carlton boss says Voss resignation proof club is in 'genuine transition'
items.description: Carlton CEO Graham Wright says the club will embark on a thorough process to determine the successor to Michael Voss.

items.title: Delta 'proud' to be at Eurovision as five nations boycott competition
items.description: This week, the Eurovision Song Contest will burst onto the stage in Vienna, and onto screens around the globe, but behind the colour and campness, this year's competition is shaping up as one of the most politically charged in history.

items.title: Six passengers from hantavirus cruise ship 'in good health', minister says
items.description: Six passengers from a cruise ship at the centre of the deadly hantavirus outbreak are "in good health", as the Australian government remains hopeful it will finalise plans to repatriate them within 48 hours.

items.title: Inside the US blockbuster that brought $68 million to the Gold Coast
items.description: The $110 million Mortal Kombat sequel is the next in a laundry list of productions putting Queensland on the radar for international films.

items.title: Australian paratrooper killed after mid-air collision during training
items.description: Warrant Officer Class Two Lachlan Muddle, a highly qualified special forces sniper and military free-fall parachutist, has died after a mid-air collision with another paratrooper during an army training exercise.

items.title: Canvas developer Instructure says 'agreement' reached with hackers
items.description: The company at the centre of a cyber attack involving online learning platform Canvas, which is used right across Australia,  says it has reached an "agreement" with the hackers responsible.

items.title: Four more ANU council members quit after Julie Bishop's shock resignation
items.description: The acting chancellor of the Australian National University confirms four more members of the university council have resigned, following last week's exit of former chancellor Julie Bishop.

items.title: 'Leaks in the urinals': Political journalism's backstory flushed out at Old Parliament House
items.description: The new Press Gallery exhibition takes visitors inside the original working spaces at Old Parliament House where reporters worked between 1927 and 1988.

items.title: Year 7 student trapped under train had bag snagged by mirror, school says
items.description: The St Aloysius College student remains in a serious condition in hospital after the incident yesterday afternoon.

items.title: Rankine says he has 'come a long way' since homophobic slur ban
items.description: After being forced to sit out of last year's finals series thanks to a suspension for a homophobic slur, Izak Rankine is confident he has grown.
